issues.legal_issue: Daughters excluded from inheritance by a customary rule become heirs when succession opens after the Hindu Succession Act has superseded that rule.
material_facts: The deceased was governed by a custom that prevented his daughters from inheriting the agricultural property.
A pre-Act declaratory decree provided that a share of the property would pass to the next reversioner, while the deceased was alive.
The deceased died after the Hindu Succession Act came into force, and his daughters claimed the property as heirs.
issues.conclusion: The daughters were the preferential heirs under the Hindu Succession Act, and the collateral heirs could not succeed to the property.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4 and 8 of the Hindu Succession Act, the Act supersedes a custom that excludes daughters from inheritance, and the heirs are determined when succession opens. The Court applied the reasoning in Giani Ram v. Ramji Lal, which held that persons previously unable to challenge an alienation could inherit when succession opened after the Act came into force.

predicates.appeal_in_succession_dispute: The case is an appeal concerning who inherits property when succession opens.
predicates.customary_rule_excludes_daughters: A custom governing the deceased prevented his daughters from inheriting the property.
predicates.succession_opens_after_reform_law: The property owner's death, which opens succession, occurred after a reform law governing inheritance came into force.

issues.definition: When an inheritance appeal concerns a custom excluding daughters and succession opens after a reform law takes effect, the daughters inherit under that law.

issues.legal_issue: A declaratory decree made during an owner's lifetime does not fix the identity of the eventual heir when it declares only that the next reversioner at the owner's death will take the property.
material_facts: A declaratory decree made before the Hindu Succession Act came into force addressed who would receive part of the property after the owner's death.
The decree did not give the collateral claimant an immediate right to the property; it provided for the next reversioner to take it.
The owner died after the Act came into force.
issues.conclusion: The decree left the identity of the successor to be determined when the owner died, so the heirs entitled under the law then in force could inherit.
issues.legal_principle: A decree limiting an alienation or interest to the holder's lifetime merely leaves the property to devolve upon the persons entitled when succession opens. The Court relied on Giani Ram v. Ramji Lal and applied Sections 2 and 4(1) of the Hindu Succession Act as discussed in that decision.

predicates.prior_decree_limits_successor_to_person_: An earlier decree provides that the person entitled to the property will be the successor when the owner dies.
predicates.succession_opens_after_reform_law: The property owner's death, which opens succession, occurred after a reform law governing inheritance came into force.

issues.definition: If an earlier decree leaves succession to the person entitled at the owner's death and succession opens after a reform law takes effect, that law determines who inherits.

issues.legal_issue: The intestate-succession provision applies when a male Hindu dies without a valid will, even if he lacked power to make a valid will of the property.
material_facts: The owner died without a valid will disposing of the property.
The High Court reasoned that intestate succession did not apply because the owner lacked power to bequeath the ancestral property by will.
issues.conclusion: The intestate-succession provision applied because the owner died intestate; the inability to make a valid will did not exclude its application.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8 of the Hindu Succession Act applies when a male Hindu dies intestate, whether he made no will or made an invalid will. The Court rejected the view that lack of testamentary power over the property prevents application of that provision.

predicates.deceased_died_without_valid_will: The property owner died without a valid will disposing of the property.

issues.definition: In an inheritance appeal, when the property owner died without a valid will, the intestate-succession rules apply.

issues.legal_issue: The rules concerning enlargement of a female Hindu's limited interest do not govern a dispute that concerns only who inherited the property when the owner died.
material_facts: The respondents relied on Section 14 of the Hindu Succession Act.
The dispute concerned who was the owner's heir on his death, rather than whether a female holder's existing limited interest became enlarged.
issues.conclusion: Neither subsection of Section 14 applied; the issue was who inherited under the succession provisions when the owner died.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 14(1) and 14(2) are not relevant where the question is the identity of the heir upon the owner's death. The Court instead applied Sections 4 and 8 of the Hindu Succession Act to determine succession.

predicates.dispute_concerns_identity_of_heir_at_dea: The parties dispute who inherited the property when its owner died, rather than the scope of a female holder's existing interest.

issues.definition: When an inheritance appeal concerns only the identity of the heir at the owner's death, analysis of enlargement of a limited interest does not apply.
